text:
Nazem Kadri is 36, back in Colorado where he won the Stanley Cup in 2022, and the Avalanche need him more than they planned to. With Nathan MacKinnon out for what's been reported as 12 weeks, the center depth behind him suddenly carries the team. Kadri has 18 points in 24 games, eight on the power play, playing a little over 18 minutes a night. He also reached 1,000 NHL games this fall, and turned the Flames' $50,000 gift to his foundation into $50,000 each for food banks in London and Calgary.

The goals are behind where they should be. He has five on 9.5 expected, the quality of his chances, shooting under 8%. He's getting the looks, and goals tend to follow chances. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking backs that up: last season he got to the home-plate area in front of the net at an 85th-percentile rate and set up teammates nearly as often.

At five on five Colorado gets 54% of the expected goals with him on the ice. His recent ice time has dipped to about 17 minutes. Watch whether that climbs now that MacKinnon is out.
headline: Kadri at 36, with more on his plate
